name: Cross-attempt staged side effect feeds a retried durable write

payload.proof_obligation: A failed statement attempt must roll back every staged side effect before a transparent retry can read it and produce durable mutations.
payload.candidate_compiler: Find statements that write a statement-staged non-durable owner and a persistent table, then intersect them with an ordinary retry producer. Route the staged value into the persistent write so duplicate application changes fresh durable truth.
payload.reject_as_variant: Another SQL spelling or transient conflict under the same StmtRollback staging owner.

provenance.introduced_for: retain a production-reachable cross-owner retry oracle after a GREEN

name: Pessimistic retry rolls back local-temporary-table mutations before replay

payload.production_workload: A settlement or migration worker loads target values into a connection-local temporary table, starts BEGIN PESSIMISTIC, and uses one multi-table UPDATE to copy the staged value into a persistent account row while advancing the staging row.
payload.natural_producer: An ordinary OLTP payment/status worker commits an update to the same persistent account after the batch statement acquired its first forUpdateTS but before it locks that row. A long join scan, a hot row, TiKV backoff, or routine storage latency widens this interval; no node failure is required.
ordering: write_conflict < OnStmtRetry < StmtRollback_first_stage < second_for_update_ts < replay_once < UPDATE_success < application_COMMIT
payload.defaults: MDL remained ON and REPEATABLE-READ remained at the session default. The test did not override tidb_pessimistic_txn_fair_locking; its resolved global value is not part of this owner proof. The only workload choice was the supported BEGIN PESSIMISTIC statement. Breakpoints paused existing boundaries and did not fabricate the competing commit or error.
payload.topology: Two ordinary SQL sessions against one current TiDB transaction engine; the ownership proof is above the storage RPC layer and needs no Region or node failure.
payload.production_outcome: TiDB transparently handles the write conflict, so the application receives UPDATE success and naturally executes its planned COMMIT. If the first temporary mutation leaked, the second attempt would persist 41 and leave temporary value 42. The fresh durable row was 40 and the session-local row was 41, exactly one application; ADMIN CHECK TABLE passed.
payload.control: The same multi-table UPDATE without a concurrent writer produced persistent value 30 and temporary value 31 in one attempt. Rolling that control transaction back restored the persistent row.
payload.holding_guard: UpdateExec stages both table mutations before pessimistic LockKeys. On lock error, handlePessimisticLockError calls StmtRollback before reopening the executor; local temporary data is copied to the session owner only at transaction commit.
payload.reopen_only_if: A side effect is published outside the statement staging owner before retry, or a retry/fallback path reopens the executor without StmtRollback covering that owner.

provenance.introduced_for: close a supported temporary-table retry candidate with a concrete production schedule

environment.runner: go test with TiDB failpoint rewrite

evidence.boundary: UpdateExec completed statement staging before KeysNeedToLock/LockKeys; the ordinary competitor commit caused the existing pessimistic retry path
evidence.control: no-conflict transaction observed temporary/persistent 31/30, then rolled back
evidence.durable_truth: after one transparent retry and application COMMIT, temporary/persistent were 41/40 rather than leaked 42/41; ADMIN CHECK TABLE passed

rationale: The local-temporary-table owner is covered by statement staging and rollback before executor replay; search next for owners outside that rollback closure.
